subject: kv example: answer a do whose operation a snapshot covers
evidence: Liveness bug in the repo's own example Go code: after snapshots were enabled (S-r), a replica installing a snapshot never answered waiters whose op the snapshot covered, so do() hung. refuting_execution: Not a spec refutation (liveness): replica 3 proposes while partitioned, others commit and compact past it, heal sends MsgSnap; replica 3's do() blocks forever. A Go test with partition + compaction + catch-up (TestSnapshotCatchUp extended) shows it; a fuzzer with partitions and a timeout would too.

subject: D21 M6: at-most-once firing of a client write (D20 (b))
spec_files: (+15 client/grpc specs: retry interceptor, dial, New, NewKV, kv.Do, kv.Put, ...)
evidence: The top-level put theorem is strengthened from a persistent update (□ ▷ Spec) to an ordinary one fired at most once (reqPre/kvReqPre), restricted to clients with MaxUnaryRetries=1 (isEtcdConn1, etcdInterceptorOk1, clientKVOnce). It ripples down to raft: Step/Propose posts return per-proposal tickets (stTks), because the model's persistent isMessage MsgProp let a leader step a proposal twice. Deciding the top-level theorem (at-most-once vs. persistent) at P0 would have fixed the shape of all these specs at once.

subject: mvcc: a generation's created revision is its main revision in the model (restore plan R3, step 1)
evidence: Old posts returned the created revision as a function of the log (kiGetVal ki atRev e; creates = map revVal of rangeTaken). The new posts exist-quantify the sub-revision (cs; cl with cl.map Main = ...), and restore takes created.main. Reason: put records the full revision of a generation's first change, while restore sets sub-revision 0, so the same log gives different values. Surfaced when the scope widened to restore (plan R3).
refuting_execution: A key first created inside a multi-op txn at sub-revision > 0 (e.g. a Txn that puts k1 then k2: k2 created at {main: r, sub: 1}), then the store is restored from the backend (restart, kvstore.restore -> keyIndex.restore). treeIndex.Get/Range on k2 then returns created {r, 0}, where before the restart it returned {r, 1}: the old spec's single log-determined value fails on one of the two. etcd's mvcc restore tests (TestRestoreContinueUnfinishedCompaction, TestKVRestore-style put/txn/reopen) or a fuzzer of txns plus restart would produce it, if the traces record keyIndex/treeIndex results with sub-revisions.

subject: auth E2w: NewServer.specM over the mode's KV invariant (kvInvM on); mode-on proposal update
evidence: kvInv, srvEr and srvBuilt become mode-indexed kvInvM on / srvErM on / srvBuiltG on. Composing the top-level theorem with on = true (P1 glue) shows the unsatisfiable precondition without any proof of NewServer.

subject: partitions S1/S2: rafthttp's CutPeer/MendPeer axioms, EtcdServer.CutPeer/MendPeer proved; the transport's remotes (D24)

refuting_execution: Transport.AddRemote(id, urls); Transport.CutPeer(id); Transport.CutPeer(id) panics in the Go code, which the planned axiom (returns on any started transport) contradicts. A Go bug, already recorded in issues/. Probably no existing rafthttp test calls CutPeer twice on a remote; a simple API-sequence fuzzer over AddRemote/CutPeer/MendPeer would find it quickly. Here P2 would test a planned trust-boundary axiom, not a proved spec.
